chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, concerning:
One who has intercourse with his wife's slave-girl without her permission is subject to the like of what is upon the fornicator: he is to be flogged one hundred lashes.

He said: “And he is not stoned if he commits zina with a Jewish woman, a Christian woman, or a slave-woman. But if he commits illicit intercourse with a free woman while he has a free wife, then stoning is upon him.”

And he said: “Just as a slave-woman, a Christian woman, and a Jewish woman do not render him muḥṣan if he commits zina with a free woman, likewise the penalty of the muḥṣan is not upon him if he commits zina with a Jewish woman, a Christian woman, or a slave-woman while he has a free woman under him.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: His statement عليه السلام, “Just as a slave-woman and a Jewish woman do not render him muḥṣan if he commits zina with a free woman, likewise the penalty of the muḥṣan is not upon him if he commits zina,” may bear the meaning that these women do not render him muḥṣan when they are with him by way of mutʿah rather than a permanent marriage contract and ownership, because mutʿah does not establish iḥṣān according to us. That which indicates this is what Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated in the report that we mentioned previously.

key_terms.حَدُّ الْمُحْصَنِ: the legal punishment applicable to a muḥṣan
key_terms.وَلِيدَةَ: a slave-girl owned by the wife
key_terms.يُرْجَمُ: he is stoned as a legal hadd punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on zina involving a slave-woman, a Jewish woman, or a Christian woman, and when does iḥṣān apply?
ai.summary: This report discusses legal rulings concerning zina and the distinction between cases involving a free woman, a slave-woman, and women from the People of the Book. It also addresses the legal meaning of iḥṣān and includes Shaykh al-Ṭūsī’s clarification that the passage may refer to cases of mutʿah, which in this context does not establish iḥṣān.
